$comment: English display overlay for the labels (§218) of this package of the Constitution of the Republic of Kazakhstan (DECISION-0070). The file is not compiled into the CLIR and is read only by the presentation layer (verbalize --labels, the MCP resource law://<package>/verbalized/en, the workbench). The translation is a working one made by the formaliser from the Russian labels of the package, checked against the authentic Russian and Kazakh texts of the Constitution; it is not an official publication, hence the status "translation" for every entry. Spelling is British. A key is the local name of the declaration (the part of the node id after "#").

Amendment.text: amendment or addition to the Constitution

AmendmentMayBeSubmitted1995.text: Article 91, paragraph 3 (1995 version). Without a positive conclusion of the Constitutional Court, amendments are submitted neither to a referendum nor to Parliament

AmendmentMayBeSubmitted1995/unless/0.text: Article 91, paragraph 3 (1995 version). Without a positive conclusion of the Constitutional Court, amendments are submitted neither to a referendum nor to Parliament

AmendmentReferendumDoubleThreshold.text: Article 92, paragraph 3. The amendment is adopted if more than half of those taking part voted for it in not less than two-thirds of the regions, the cities of republican significance and the capital

AmendmentViolatesEntrenchedCore1995.text: Article 91, paragraph 2 (1995 version). The independence, unitary character and territorial integrity of the Republic, its form of government, the fundamental principles, the seven-year term of the President and the single election of the President are unalterable

Constitution1995InForceOnPublication.text: Article 90, paragraph 1 (1995 version). The Constitution comes into force on the day the results of the referendum are officially published, with the simultaneous termination of the previously adopted Constitution

ConstitutionalConclusion.text: conclusion of the Constitutional Court on the conformity of an amendment to the requirements of the Constitution

EffectiveDateAppointmentTwoMonths.text: Article 95. A transitional appointment whose time limit runs from the day the Constitution comes into force is made within two months

EntrenchmentConclusion.text: Article 93. The conclusion of the Constitutional Court is positive if the amendment conforms to the requirements of Article 2, paragraph 7 and Article 43, paragraph 5

EntrenchmentConclusion1995.text: Article 91, paragraph 3 (1995 version). Amendments are submitted to a referendum or to Parliament where there is a conclusion of the Constitutional Court that they conform to the requirements of paragraph 2

ExistingActsContinueIfCompatible.text: Article 96, paragraph 1. Statutes and other regulatory legal acts in force on the day the Constitution comes into force apply in so far as they do not contradict it

ExistingActsContinueIfCompatible/unless/.text: Article 96, paragraph 1. Statutes and other regulatory legal acts in force on the day the Constitution comes into force apply in so far as they do not contradict it

FirstKurultaiElectionTransition.text: Article 95, paragraph 1. Elections to the Kurultai are called within one month and held within two months of the day the Constitution comes into force

FirstSessionAppointmentTwoMonths.text: Article 95, paragraphs 2–4. Transitional appointments are made within two months of the day the first session of the Kurultai of the first convocation opens

IncumbentContinuity.text: Article 95. Until the new compositions are formed, the incumbent office-holders retain their powers

LegalAct.text: a statute or another regulatory legal act

ListIsNotASubjectReading.text: reading A of Article 91, paragraph 2: the list protects subjects but not itself

ListItselfEntrenchedReading.text: reading B of Article 91, paragraph 2: the unalterability of the list is a fundamental principle

NarrowingAmendmentFilter1995.text: a narrowing amendment may be submitted where the court has given its conclusion, provided the narrowing is not held to be an encroachment on the core

NarrowingAmendmentFilter1995/unless/0.text: a narrowing amendment may be submitted where the court has given its conclusion, provided the narrowing is not held to be an encroachment on the core

NarrowingOutsideCore1995.text: reading A: the list in paragraph 2 is not itself a protected subject, and narrowing it is an ordinary amendment

NarrowingTouchesCore1995.text: reading B: the unalterability of the list in paragraph 2 is a fundamental principle, and narrowing it encroaches on the core

NewConstitutionInForceFromJulyFirst.text: Article 94, paragraph 1. The Constitution comes into force on 1 July 2026

OldActsApplyIfCompatible1995.text: Article 92, paragraph 4 (1995 version). The legislation in force at the moment the Constitution comes into force applies in so far as it does not contradict it

OldConstitutionRepealedSimultaneously.text: Article 94, paragraph 1. The previously adopted Constitution ceases to have effect simultaneously with the coming into force of the new one

ParliamentaryAmendmentFourFifths1995.text: Article 91, paragraph 1 (1995 version). If the President declines Parliament's proposal for a referendum, Parliament may, by a majority of not less than four-fifths of the total number of the deputies of each of the Chambers, adopt a statute introducing amendments to the Constitution

ParliamentaryAmendmentLaw.text: statute of Parliament on amendments and additions to the Constitution (1995 version)

PositiveConclusionRequiredForReferendum.text: Article 93. The amendment is submitted to a national referendum where there is a positive conclusion of the Constitutional Court

ReferendumTurnoutMoreThanHalf.text: Article 92, paragraph 2. The national referendum has taken place if more than half of the citizens entitled to take part in it have voted

TransitionalAppointment.text: appointment made in the transitional period
